RaghavanBareinboim2026CTFIDUPlus proves identification completeness but gives no acquisition-certificate transcript-size theorem.
RaghavanBareinboim2026CTFIDUPlus, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 3.5, operate on a fixed collection of concrete input distributions and do not establish assignment-uniform source sparsification.
CourcelleMosbah1993MSOEvaluations and ArnborgLagergrenSeese1991TreeDecomposable provide the metatheory, not a cost-preserving physical-protocol interpretation with this incidence width.
RaghavanBareinboim2026CTFIDUPlus fixes Layer-3 inputs, while AkbariEtesamiKiyavash2022MinCost optimizes ordinary interventions; neither gives the proposed physical Layer-2.5 certificate problem.
AkbariEtesamiKiyavash2022MinCost already proves singleton reduction and hedge-hitting for ordinary intervention design; the SELECT--RAND--READ embedding is a scoped semantic lift.

novelty_flags.label: Theorem 2 (ordinary-subclass equivalence), gap
novelty_flags.one_line: The gap attributes ordinary-design hardness to Akbari et al. (2022), Theorem 1 and Lemma 3, but Theorem 1 is the singleton no-more-costly reduction and hardness is Theorem 2; Lemma 3 is the hedge-hitting equivalence.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 1 (cost-optimal certificate)
soundness_flags.one_line: The theorem asserts existence and computation of E⋆ under conditions that permit infeasibility; split it into a feasible-case optimum statement and an infeasibility alternative.

soundness_flags.label: Theorem 2 (ordinary-subclass equivalence)
soundness_flags.one_line: The accepting certificate E is neither quantified nor constructed from B1,…,Bt and their slices, so Acc(Q,E;G)=1 is not a determinate claim.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4--5, Algorithm 2 and Theorem 3.5; p. 4, Lemmas 3.3--3.4
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Algorithm 2 takes an un-nested counterfactual query and input distribution specifications; Theorem 3.5 gives CTFIDU+ soundness and completeness, while Lemmas 3.3--3.4 establish ctf-hedge nonidentifiability and IDENTIFY+ completeness.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 5, Algorithm 1 and Theorem 3.5; p. 4, Assumption 3.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: CTF-REALIZE returns a sample iff the Layer-3 distribution is realizable, under the stated one-execution-per-mechanism physical constraint.

Theorem 1 reduces a connected-target collection to a no-more-costly singleton intervention; Theorem 2 supplies the polynomial reduction proving NP-hardness; Lemma 3 equates the connected-target problem to minimum-weight hedge hitting.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 2, contributions; pp. 4--5, weighted partial Max-SAT and ILP formulation
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper reformulates ordinary minimum-cost intervention design as weighted partial Max-SAT and integer linear programming and gives faster exact algorithms for that problem.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Repair Theorem 2 by defining an explicit map from an ordinary identifying collection (B_i) and its finite label set to E_B, then state Acc(Q,E_B;G)=1 and both cost identities for that named certificate.
Correct the Akbari comparison: cite Theorem 1 for singleton reduction, Lemma 3 for hedge hitting, and Theorem 2 for NP-hardness; make the embedding's strict semantic delta the stated novelty.

Elevate the central result by proving a strict class relation between ordinary designs and a nonempty Layer-2.5 protocol class, with the positive separation as the witness and the full-incidence compiler as the constructive decision procedure.

recommended_next_step: Revise the two ill-posed theorem statements and the Akbari attribution, then retain the coupled uniform-certificate and full-incidence compilation kernel for Stage 0.
